Illegal move? The cow tries, comes back, and a message says why. Hints explain themselves.
Beat each computer level with each colour for a star. The daily puzzle is the same for all.
Auto Play (free, silent): watch a full game play itself - it pauses for you to think, then reveals and plays the move it chose.

title: Mū Tōrere
tagline: The eight-pointed star game of Aotearoa
description: Mū Tōrere is a traditional Māori board game of Aotearoa New Zealand. Four stones each sit on an eight-pointed star around a central pit, the putahi: slide one stone at a time and leave your opponent with no move. The game is tiny and fully solved, all traps and foresight. Learn in eight hands-on lessons, watch free Auto Play play a whole game for you, climb a Ladder of twelve opponents, solve a new proven puzzle daily, or play a friend on one phone. Carved-wood board, shell and greenstone stones, calm sound. An in-app Rules page spells out every move. No ads, works offline.
howToPlay: New here? Eight short lessons teach every move, or watch free Auto Play play a whole game for you.
TAP one of your stones (its legal points glow), then TAP a point. Or DRAG the stone there.
A stone moves one step: to the next point around the star, or between the rim and the putahi (centre).
A stone may enter the putahi only when it stands beside an enemy stone. From the putahi it may step to any empty point.
You win when your opponent has no legal move. The same position three times is a draw.
Move not allowed? The stone tries, comes back, and a message tells you why.
Hint shows a good move and why (3 per game). Take back undoes your move and the reply.
Climb the Ladder of 12 opponents. The last two cannot be beaten, only held to a draw.

title: Nonogram
tagline: Fill the grid. Reveal the picture.
description: A calm logic picture puzzle: use the numbers beside the grid to decide which squares are filled and a small illustration appears. 121 pictures from 5 by 5 to 20 by 20, each with exactly one solution that logic alone can reach. Think explains the next step in plain words, Watch & Learn solves pictures with the reasons shown, and a daily picture keeps it fresh. English and Japanese. No timer, no ads.
howToPlay: The numbers beside each row and above each column give the lengths of the runs of filled squares in that line.
Tap a square to fill it, or drag along a line to fill a run. Use Cross to mark squares you know are empty.
Think finds the next square that logic proves and explains why. Use Zoom and Move on big boards.
Every picture earns up to three stars: solved, no Think, no wrong marks.
Learn and Watch & Learn teach overlap, edges and gaps step by step.

title: Noughts & Crosses
tagline: Three in a row, made deep.
description: The classic three-in-a-row game, made beautiful: lit bronze crosses and verdigris noughts on carved marble, with four ways to play. Classic 3x3, the Roman Terni Lapilli with sliding pieces, Misère where three in a row loses, and a 4x4 Quad board. Five opponent levels up to a solver that never slips, two players on one phone, Think with a plain-English reason, eleven lessons and Watch & Learn. No timers and no ads.
genre: abstract strategy, three in a row
howToPlay: Take turns with your opponent placing your mark. X always goes first. Three in a row wins.
Tap an empty square to place your mark. A full board with no line is a draw.
Terni Lapilli: place three pieces each, then tap a piece and a joined empty point to slide it. Diagonals count.
Misère: complete three in a row and you lose. Quad: four in a row, or a 2x2 square, wins on the 4x4 board.
Think shows the best move and why: this blocks a fork, this wins. Undo takes a move back.
Learn teaches threats, blocks and forks in eleven short lessons. Watch & Learn plays whole games with time to think and a Pause button.

title: O An Quan: Mandarin Squares
tagline: Vietnam's pebble game of sowing and capture.
description: The traditional Vietnamese children's game, rebuilt on a lacquered wooden board: sow stones one at a time, relay through full squares, leap an empty square to capture and win the two mandarins. Five opponent levels, two players on one phone, Think with a reason in words, six lessons and Watch & Learn. Play in English or in Vietnamese. No timers and no ads.
howToPlay: Tap one of your squares that holds stones, then choose Sow left or Sow right (or swipe from the square).
Your stones are dropped one by one. If the last one lands before a full square, pick that square up and sow on.
If the last stone is followed by an empty square and then a full one, you capture the full one. Chains count.
The two big mandarin stones are worth 10 points each. The game ends when both are captured; the higher total wins.
Run out of stones and you refill your side from your winnings. Think shows the best move and why.

title: Oche Darts 501
tagline: Hold steady, release, and check out on a double.
description: Pub darts with a drifting aim point that tightens then tires. Race down from 501 with a proper double-out, learn finishes with the checkout coach, and play five opponents or a friend.
howToPlay: Touch and hold to aim: the aim point sways, then settles, then tires.
Let go while the aim point is over your target.
Three darts a visit; each dart is subtracted from 501.
Finish exactly on zero with a double, or you bust.
Tap Think for the best next dart and checkout route.

title: Okey Offline
tagline: Turkey's tile rummy, four at the table.
description: Okey is the tile rummy game of Turkey. You and three computer players share 106 tiles; each deal a turned-up indicator decides which tile is the wild okey for that deal only. Draw, arrange your two-row rack into runs and sets (or seven pairs) by dragging, then finish by discarding your last tile. Finish on the okey itself and the deal counts double. Sort helpers tidy the rack, a free Hint explains its reasoning, and Watch & Learn plays a whole deal with time to think before each move. Three computer levels, a full Rules page, English or Turkish labels. Offline, no ads, score only.
howToPlay: Four players, 106 tiles. A turned-up indicator makes the next tile up in that colour the wild okey for this deal.
Your turn: DRAW from the face-down stack, or TAP the glowing pile on your left to take your neighbour's last discard.
ARRANGE your rack by DRAGGING tiles between its two rows. A green line shows every valid run or set.
Runs are 3+ consecutive tiles of one colour (12-13-1 is allowed). Sets are 3 or 4 tiles of one number in different colours.
DISCARD one tile: drag it onto your own pile, or tap it and press Discard.
Finish when the 14 tiles you keep are all in runs and sets, or form seven pairs. Finishing on the okey doubles the deal.
Runs, Sets and Smart sort the rack for you. Hint is free and explains its choice.
Watch & Learn plays a whole deal for you with time to think before each move, and a Pause that freezes it any moment.

title: One Arrow Oath
tagline: Nothing fires twice.
description: A deckbuilder where your best cards can be played only once. You are an archer sworn never to loose the same arrow twice: every named Arrow you play is spent for the whole run, so each fight asks how little you can afford to spend. Read every enemy's intent, answer it with the right element, take on Debts that come due at the worst moment, and decide whether to keep the Covenant or break it. Inspired by a warrior's vow from ancient Sanskrit epic poetry, one of the world's oldest literary traditions. The world and every name in it are original. An in-app Rules page covers every system.
howToPlay: Read the intent above each enemy: what it will do this turn, and which element answers it.
Press a card and pull it down like a bowstring, then release to play it. Tapping it twice also works.
Gold-framed Arrows hit hard and are spent for the whole run. Steel-framed Techniques come back.
Answer an attack with the element that beats it. A Ward cancels it; a matching Arrow also strikes for +50%.
Finish weak enemies with Reed Shafts. Never loose a named Arrow at a Lure - it will be wasted.
After each fight, take one new card. Camps heal, the Tuner trades, Envoys offer choices.
Debts give power now and come due in the final fight. Settle them at a Camp if you can.
Breaking the Covenant wins the moment, but Standing lost that way is hard to earn back.
New to it all? Tap Auto Play on the title screen to watch a whole run play itself, at a thinking pace you choose.

title: Origami: Fold by Fold
tagline: Fold paper into something wonderful.
description: Real, curling, layered paper in 3D. Grab a flap, drag it across and feel the crease snap flat, then watch your kite, puppy, fish or paper dart stand up. Seven models, six washi papers, free-fold Studio and a Watch & Learn mode that folds for you. No ads and no timers.
howToPlay: Each model is a short list of folds. The caption tells you the next one.
Grab the glowing corner and drag it across the dashed crease to the ring.
Let go past halfway and it lands flat; let go early and it springs back.
Neatness scores how close your finger ended to the ring. Folds are always exact.
Some steps unfold the last fold, turn the paper over or fold only the top layer.
Press Hint to see the fold as a ghost demonstration. Three stars for neat folds and no hints.
Studio lets you fold freely; Watch & Learn folds whole models for you.

title: Oud Maqam Strings
tagline: Slide to the quarter-tone, pluck in time.
description: Play the oud, the fretless pear-shaped lute of the Arab world. Slide a finger along the bare neck to land on the right pitch, including the quarter-tones of Rast and Bayati, and pluck in time over rhythm cycles. Learn six original pieces phrase by phrase, perform them while the room lights up and an ensemble joins in, watch the computer play with a ghost finger that explains each note, or improvise a taqsim in free play.
howToPlay: Rings on the neck show where each note is. Touch the neck at the ring on the beat to pluck.
Keep your finger down and slide to bend the note or land on a second ring.
To repeat a note, hold your finger still and tap the wooden body with your other hand.
Turquoise diamonds on the neck mark quarter-tones, notes between piano keys.
Learn the phrases: listen, then echo each phrase of a piece.
Perform the whole piece for stars; play cleanly and more instruments join in.
Watch and Learn shows a ghost finger and says why each note sits where it does.
Free play has a drone, rhythm and a journey guide for a taqsim.

title: Oware
tagline: The seed-sowing game of West Africa
description: Oware is the classic seed-sowing game of Ghana and West Africa, part of the mancala family. Twelve pits, forty-eight seeds: lift a pit, sow seeds round the board, and capture pits that end with two or three. Learn in eight short hands-on lessons, watch free Auto Play play a whole game at your own pace, play the computer at five levels from Easy to Grandmaster, pass the phone to a friend, and solve a new capture puzzle every day. Hand-carved wood and glossy seed art, large text and reduced motion. Full rules are in the in-app Rules page. No ads, works offline.
howToPlay: New here? Eight short lessons teach every move, or watch free Auto Play play a whole game at your own pace.
TAP one of your pits on the bottom row to sow it. Glowing pits are the ones you can play.
Seeds go one per pit, counter-clockwise: along your row, then back along your opponent's row.
If your last seed makes an opponent pit hold 2 or 3, you capture it, and the pits before it if they also hold 2 or 3.
A pit with 12 or more seeds laps the board and skips its own pit.
If your opponent has no seeds you must play a move that gives them some.
First to capture 25 seeds wins. Undo takes back a move; Hint (3 per game) shows a good move and why.
Daily puzzle: TAP the one pit that captures the most seeds. Same puzzle for everyone.

title: Pachisi
tagline: The royal race of the cross
description: Pachisi is the royal race game of India, ancestor of Ludo. Throw six cowrie shells, count the mouths that face up, and race four pawns around the embroidered cloth cross to its centre. Land on a rival to send it home, hide on the marked squares, block the way with a pair. Play the full game or the friendly Ludo mode, with two to four players, against four computer personalities or friends passing one phone. Nine hands-on lessons, Auto Play (a full game plays itself at a pace you set), a daily race and an exhaustive in-app Rules reference. No ads, works offline.
howToPlay: New here? Nine short lessons teach every move, or watch free Auto Play play a whole game at your own pace.
TAP the cowries, or SWIPE up across them, to throw. Count the mouths facing up: 1 up = 10, 2 = 2, 3 = 3, 4 = 4, 5 = 25, 6 = 6, none = 12.
Grace throws (10, 25, 6, 12) give another throw and are the only throws that let a waiting pawn enter the board.
Pawns that can move glow. TAP one to see where it lands, then TAP it again to move it. A pawn that cannot move shakes and tells you why.
Race anticlockwise once around the cross, then up the middle lane to the centre. The centre needs an exact count.
Land exactly on a rival pawn to send it home. Squares marked with an X are safe; two of your pawns on one square form a block.
Play 2, 3 or 4 players against computers (Beginner, Cautious, Balanced, Bold) or pass one phone between friends.
Ludo mode uses one die and a smaller board. The daily race sets the same six throws for everybody.

title: Paper Cutting
tagline: Fold, snip, unfold: one cut repeats all around.
description: Fold coloured paper in half, quarters or twelfths, snip the wedge with scissors or punches, then unfold it in real 3D to reveal the pattern. 26 levels from paper-cutting traditions around the world, a free-cutting Studio and Gallery, and a Watch & Learn mode that explains every cut. No ads and no timers.
howToPlay: Pick a fold: the paper folds itself into one small wedge.
Snip the wedge with Scissors (drag around a shape) or Punch (tap to stamp a shape).
A cut on a fold edge opens into one whole shape; a cut at the centre becomes the middle.
Press Unfold and watch the pattern appear. Stars reward a close match with few cuts.
Refold to keep cutting, Undo the last cut, or ask for a Hint.
Studio is free cutting; the Gallery keeps your cut-outs; Watch & Learn explains each cut.

title: Parqués: Salida y Cárcel
tagline: Colombian parqués: break out of jail, split your dice, capture rivals
description: Colombia's version of the pachisi family. Free your pieces from the cárcel with a pair of dice, spend each die on the piece you choose, hide on seguros, build barriers and send rivals back to jail. Play 1-3 computer opponents or pass one phone around the table, get hints, or watch a whole game with Auto Play.
howToPlay: Roll two dice: tap or swipe the tray.
Only a pair frees a piece from the cárcel onto your salida.
Each die is its own move: pick a die, then a glowing piece.
Land exactly on a rival outside a safe square to send it to jail.
Two of your pieces on one square form a barrier rivals cannot pass.
Bring all four pieces up your lane to the corona to win.

title: Pearl Diving
tagline: A season on a Gulf pearling boat, one breath at a time.
description: Sail with a Muharraq dive crew in the summer of 1924. Sing, dive on one breath, haul your partner up, open the shells at dusk and decide what to sell, repay and keep for a necklace.
howToPlay: Plan each dawn: pick a pearl bank or a rest day
Hold to breathe in, let go in the green band, then dive
Tap shell beds and time the closing ring, signal before air runs low
Haul your partner up on the beat, open the shells, grade the pearls
Sell or hold at the harbour, repay the advance, help your family

title: Peg Solitaire
tagline: Jump. Capture. Leave just one.
description: The classic jumping puzzle from the French court, on a lit wooden board with glass pegs. Five boards (Triangle, English, French, Diamond, Grand Cross), 60 curated puzzles with stars and par, a Daily puzzle, hints from a solver and Auto Play that shows a full solution. No clock, no ads, works offline.
howToPlay: Tap a peg: golden holes show where it can jump. Tap one, or drag the peg there.
A jump goes in a straight line over one neighbouring peg into an empty hole. The peg you jumped is removed.
On the Triangle board pegs can also jump along both diagonals.
If the same peg can jump again it stays lifted, so chain jumps in one move.
Leave one peg for three stars, two for two, three or four for one.
Stuck? Undo as often as you like, or ask for a Hint: it shows a real route to one peg.
Puzzles open one after another on five boards. The Daily puzzle is the same for everyone.
Auto Play shows a whole game solved, with pause and adjustable think time.

title: Pelota Vasca
tagline: Hit the wall. Read the angles. Win to 22.
description: The fast wall ball of the Basque Country in real 3D. Play one on one or two on two with the bare hand or a paddle, aim at the front and left walls, and time your swing. Five rivals, Learn lessons, Think hints and Watch & Learn.
howToPlay: Drag to run, or let Auto-run take you to the ball.
Tap the wall to aim; choose Drive, Drop or Lob.
Press SWING when the ring closes around the button.
Use the left wall and the rebote; the ball may bounce once.
Win to 22 against five rival levels.

title: Perch
tagline: Read the stone. Choose your moment.
description: You are a small bird on a branch, and hunters with catapults ring the field. You never aim: you read the stone coming and choose your moment to fly. Survive each day until sunset for up to three stars. Level 1 is one tree; from level 2 whole groves and orchards open up and you choose where to fly. Every level adds one new idea: golden seeds, fast archers, wind, a Master Hunter with a pattern to learn, nets and beaters. From level 3, close calls earn acorns to knock hunters flat. A hit only ruffles feathers. No ads, works offline. An in-game Rules page covers every mechanic in detail.
howToPlay: A hunter pulls back a catapult and a red ring shows the perch the stone will hit. A dotted arc shows its path.
Level 1: tap anywhere to fly and the bird picks the safest perch. From level 2, tap the perch you want to fly to.
Leave at the last moment for a close call (+5). Dodges in a row build a combo up to x5.
You have 3 feathers. Survive until the bar at the top fills (sunset): 3 stars for no hits.
Golden seeds: tap the perch that holds one to fly for it. Every third seed heals a feather.
Archers fire fast arrows. In wind, trust the red ring, not the hunter. Nets cover a whole tree: leave it. Beaters rattle your perch.
Hit back (level 3+): close calls earn acorns, up to 3. Tap a hunter to knock him down and cancel his shot.
Boss levels: the Master Hunter fires the same pattern every attempt. Learn it.

title: Pick-up Sticks
tagline: Lift one. Don't wobble the rest.
description: The gentle game of a steady hand. Slide lacquered sticks out of a heap one at a time without moving any other, collect bamboo, jade, red lacquer and the golden master, and outplay five rivals, the Solo Ladder and the Daily Heap.
howToPlay: Press a free stick (nothing lying across it) and slide it slowly out of the heap.
Let go once it is clear. Bamboo is worth 1, indigo 3, jade 5, red lacquer 10, the golden master 20.
If any other stick moves too far, it is a fault and the turn passes.
Win the golden master to use the lever and sweep sticks aside.
Take turns against a rival, climb the ladder or play the Daily Heap.

title: Pond Hockey Slide
tagline: Slide a skater. Strike the puck. Score on the pond.
description: Shinny on a frozen pond, turn by turn. Pull back like a slingshot and slide a skater into the puck, bank it off the snowbanks, dodge loose snow drifts and outplay four computer rivals.
howToPlay: Press one of your skaters and pull back like a slingshot, then let go.
Pull length sets the power and pull direction sets the aim; a dotted line shows the glide.
Strike the puck so the whole puck crosses the goal line between the posts.
Snow drifts slow anything that crosses them; the banks bounce skaters and puck.
First to 3 goals (or 5 in a full match) wins; ties go to sudden death.

title: Pottery Wheel
tagline: Throw, shape and glaze a pot on a spinning wheel.
description: A calm craft game: centre a lump of clay, open it, pull the walls up and shape the form with your fingertip in real 3D, then trim, glaze and fire it. Six glaze traditions from around the world, twelve target-outline challenges, a daily pot, a shelf for your finished work, and Watch and Learn, which throws a whole pot for you and explains each stroke. No ads, works offline.
howToPlay: Centre: press a finger against the side the clay swings towards and hold steady.
Open: press down in the middle, then draw outwards to make room.
Pull: press into the wall and slide up it, slowly. The wall thins and the pot rises.
Shape: drag the wall out for a belly, in for a neck. In Challenges, match the ghost outline.
Trim: smooth the outside and press near the base for a foot.
Glaze: pick a tradition and hold the brush on the turning pot to paint bands.
Fire the kiln and put your pot on the shelf.
Stuck? Hint shows the next touch; Watch and Learn throws a whole pot for you.

title: Quilt Patterns
tagline: Piece traditional quilt blocks and design a quilt, one fabric at a time.
description: A calm design puzzle about quilting. Stitch printed fabrics into six traditional blocks, meet briefs about contrast, balance and repeat, then arrange blocks into a quilt top with sashing and a border. Lessons, hints that explain, a Squint tool for value, Free Studio and a Gallery.
howToPlay: Tap a fabric in the tray, then tap or drag across the pieces of the block.
Meet every rule on the brief card, or copy the sample exactly.
Use Squint to see light and dark, and the bulb for a hint that explains.
Arrange finished blocks into a quilt, then add sashing and a border.
Watch and Learn designs a block and a quilt and explains each choice.

title: Rayuela
tagline: Toss the tejo. Hop the beat. Reach the sky.
description: Rayuela is the chalk-and-stone hopping game played in courtyards and streets across Latin America and Spain, also called avion, golosa and luche. Toss your tejo onto the next number, hop the course on the beat with one foot on singles and two on doubles, rest in the Sky square, and pick the tejo up on the way back without touching a line. Three courses, four computer levels, two players, Learn, Practice and Watch & Learn.
howToPlay: Tap TOSS to lock the sideways aim, then again to throw the tejo into the next numbered square.
After four drum beats, tap on every beat as the ring closes: one foot on a single square, TWO FEET on a double.
Land in the Sky square with two feet, turn, and hop back the same way.
Just before your tejo, tap PICK UP on the beat, then hop on and out of the course.
A tap that is too early or too late lands on a line and ends your turn. Finish the numbers first to win.

title: Five in a Row: Renju & Omok
tagline: Gomoku, Renju and Omok with a strong AI and a coach.
description: Make five in a row to win. Three authentic rule sets (free-style Gomoku, Renju with Black's restrictions and optional tournament openings, and Korean Omok), five computer levels, a coach that explains every threat, eight lessons and a Watch & Learn mode. Lit wooden boards, portrait and landscape.
howToPlay: Touch the board to aim a ghost stone, slide to adjust, lift to place it.
Be the first to line up five stones: across, up and down, or diagonally.
In Renju, Black needs exactly five and may not make an overline, a double four or a double three.
Omok is played on a 19 by 19 board and bans Black's double three.
Red crosses mark Black's forbidden points; gold and red rings mark fives to make or stop.
Use Hint for a move with a plain-words explanation, and Undo to take a move back.
Learn the key patterns in eight short lessons, or watch the computer play both sides.
Choose a computer level from Learner to Master, or pass the device for two players.

title: Reversi Flip Board
tagline: Trap them, turn them, take the board.
description: The classic game of flipping, beautifully made. Place a disc, trap a line of enemy discs between two of yours and watch them turn over in a ripple. Classic 8 by 8, quick Mini 6 by 6 and Reverse (fewest discs wins). Five computer levels, two players on one device, hands-on lessons, hints that explain why, take back and a Watch & Learn mode. A felt and brass board, glossy two-faced discs, large text and reduced motion options. No ads, works offline.
howToPlay: New here? Tap Learn to play: five short hands-on lessons where you make every move yourself.
Marked squares show where you may place a disc. Tap one.
Your disc must trap a straight line of enemy discs between itself and one of your own discs: along a row, a column or a diagonal.
Every trapped disc turns to your colour, in every direction at once.
If you have no legal move you pass, and the app does it for you.
Corners can never be flipped. Be careful with the squares beside an empty corner.
The game ends when neither side can move: most discs wins. In Reverse, the fewest wins.
Hint explains a good move, Take back undoes your last move, and Auto Play shows the computer playing both sides.

title: Rice Terraces
tagline: Guide the spring, share the water, bring in the gold
description: Tend a mountainside of rice terraces through a year of seasons: route the spring water with gates and channels, soak, plant, weed, mend the walls and harvest, in the Cordillera of the Philippines and in Bali. Real 3D, eight years, a growing village.
howToPlay: Tap a round gate to open or close it: water runs downhill through open gates.
Keep each field's water inside its green band; the band changes with the season.
Tap a field to plant, weed, clear snails, harvest or mend its wall.
Share the water with neighbours and the valley: fair sharing earns stars.
Think and Watch & Learn show what a farmer would do, and why.

title: Rithmomachia: Number Battle
tagline: The philosophers' game of medieval Europe, with the arithmetic on screen.
description: Rithmomachia, the battle of numbers, was a game for scholars across medieval Europe. Every piece carries a number. Touch an enemy piece whose number is equal to yours, or in the ratio 1:2, 1:3 or 2:3, and it is taken; ambush a piece between two of yours whose numbers add up to its own. Win by lining three pieces up in the enemy camp as an arithmetic, geometric or harmonic progression. Eight hands-on lessons, five computer levels, hints, danger marks, a Watch & Learn mode and the sum of every capture shown on the board. Gold leaf, lapis and vellum. No ads, works offline.
howToPlay: New here? Tap Learn to play: eight short hands-on lessons where you make every move yourself.
Tap a piece and its reachable squares glow. Rounds step one square, triangles jump two diagonally, squares leap three straight.
Touch an enemy piece whose number is equal to yours, or in the ratio 1:2, 1:3 or 2:3, and you take it.
Ambush: if your moved piece and another of yours stand in line either side of an enemy piece and add up to its number, it falls.
The board shows the sum of every capture, such as 6 : 12 = 1 : 2 or 4 + 5 = 9, so you always see why a piece fell.
Win by lining up three of your pieces in the enemy camp as an arithmetic, geometric or harmonic progression, or by taking 10 pieces.
Hint explains a good move, danger marks and a warning line show what the other side threatens, and Take back undoes a move.
Auto Play shows the computer playing both sides, with time to think and a Pause button.

title: The Royal Game of Ur
tagline: A race from the cradle of civilisation
description: The Royal Game of Ur is the Game of Twenty Squares, played in Mesopotamia over four thousand years ago. Roll four pyramid dice and race seven inlaid pieces down your lane, up the shared middle lane and home. Rosettes are safe and give another roll; landing on an enemy sends it back. Learn in nine hands-on lessons, watch Auto Play demonstrate a whole game move by move at your own pace, play four computer levels or a friend, and solve a daily best-move puzzle. Lapis, shell and red-limestone art lit by an oil lamp. Plays in portrait and landscape. No ads, works offline.
howToPlay: New here? Nine short lessons teach every move, or watch free Auto Play play a whole game at your own pace.
Tap the dice to roll four pyramid dice: each gold tip up counts 1, so a roll is 0 to 4.
Tap a glowing piece, then the glowing square it goes to. Moves are exact.
Your path: 4 squares in your lane, 8 in the shared middle lane, then 2 home. Rosettes give another roll.
Landing on an enemy piece in the middle lane sends it back. A piece on a rosette is safe.
The central rosette blocks the lane: nobody can land there while it is occupied.
A piece leaves the board only with the exact roll. First to bring all seven home wins.
Refused move? The piece tries and returns, and a message says why. Hints and Take back help.

title: Rugby Conversion
tagline: Read the wind, set the ball, strike on the beat.
description: The goal-kicking game of the conversion kick. Judge the wind and the angle, choose your ball tilt and power, then strike on the beat in a real 3D stadium. A 24-level ladder, five rival kickers, lessons, and a Watch & Learn mode that explains every kick.
howToPlay: Read the wind dial and the flag on the posts, then aim into the wind.
Pick Upright, Leaning or Flat and set the power.
Press Kick and watch the three beats of the run-up.
Flick up as the ring closes on the ball; bend the flick to curl it.
Make 2 of 3 to clear a level and climb the ladder.

title: Russian Loto: Barrels
tagline: Wooden kegs, cardboard cards, a calm race to call LOTO.
description: The family number game of Russia and the former Soviet lands. Wooden kegs numbered 1 to 90 tumble out of a linen bag; cover the called numbers on up to six cards, beat the computer players and call ROW, TWO ROWS or LOTO. Face to face, daily challenge and a Watch & Learn mode included.
howToPlay: Pick how many cards to play, from 1 to 6.
A keg tumbles out and its number is called.
Look in the matching column (1-9, 10-19 ... 80-90) and tap the number.
Each keg stays open only for a few draws, so be quick.
Press ROW, TWO ROWS or LOTO when you have it, before the computer does.

title: Sapo: Frog Toss
tagline: Toss brass discs at the open mouth of the frog.
description: The classic tavern table game of Peru, Chile and Argentina. Pull back, aim, add spin and drop brass discs into the golden frog's mouth for 400.
howToPlay: Drag down in the lower part of the screen to pull the disc back; the ring shows where it lands.
Pick a high Lob or a low Drive, and a spin to the left or right.
A disc that drops into a hole scores: the frog's mouth is worth 400.
Loose discs stay on the table: knock your rival's away.
After each round the loose disc nearest the mouth earns a bonus. Tap Think for a tested throw.

title: Scopa
tagline: The Italian card game of the broom
description: Scopa is one of Italy's three major national card games, played with a 40-card Italian deck: coins, cups, swords and batons. Match a card's rank or a sum to capture it, clear the table for a scopa, and score cards, coins, sette bello and primiera. Nine hands-on lessons, free Auto Play at your own pace, four computer levels to a card-counting Maestro, four-player partnerships, and a new daily deal every day. Original hand-drawn Italian court cards, a trattoria table, and a French-suit option. No ads, no chips, score only.
howToPlay: New here? Nine short lessons teach every move, or watch free Auto Play play a whole game at your own pace.
TAP a card in your hand, then TAP a table card of the same rank to capture it.
If several table cards add up to your card's rank, TAP each one to take the whole set.
A matching card must always be taken alone, even when a sum is also possible.
Clear the table and you score a scopa: one point, shown with a flourish (not on the round's last play).
Nothing to capture? TAP your card again to lay it on the table.
A round is scored on most cards, most coins, the sette bello and primiera. Play to 11 or 21.
Daily deal: find the single most valuable capture. Same deal for everyone, every day.

title: Seega: Desert Siege
tagline: Place. Slide. Sandwich.
description: A traditional Egyptian board game for a 5x5 board, made beautiful. Fill the board two stones at a time, leaving only the centre empty, then slide your stones and trap enemy stones between two of yours. Lit pebbles and date stones sit on a carved sandstone board. Five opponent levels from Novice to Master, two players on one phone, Think with a plain-English reason, a short Learn course and Watch & Learn. Play in English or in Arabic. No timers and no ads.
howToPlay: Each side has 12 stones. Take turns placing two stones at a time on any empty square except the centre, until the board is full.
Then slide one stone a step, up, down, left or right, into an empty square. The side that placed last moves first, into the centre.
Trap an enemy stone between two of yours, in a row or column, to capture it. One slide can take several; the same stone may go on.
Corners can never be captured and the centre square is safe too. If a side cannot move, the other side moves again.
Reduce your opponent to one stone to win. Think shows a good move and why; Learn and Watch & Learn teach the ideas.

title: Senet
tagline: The board game of ancient Egypt
description: Senet is the board game of ancient Egypt, played for thousands of years and shown in tomb paintings. Throw four sticks, race five pieces along a 30-square path, swap lone enemy pieces, hold a wall of three, and avoid the House of Water. Rules follow a widely published modern reconstruction. Learn in ten hands-on lessons, watch free Auto Play play a whole game at your own pace, play five computer levels or a friend, and solve a daily puzzle. Ebony-and-ivory board, gilded inlay, faience pieces, tumbling sticks. No ads, works offline.
howToPlay: New here? Ten short lessons teach every move, or watch free Auto Play play a whole game at your own pace.
TAP the sticks to throw. Count the light faces: 1 to 4, or 5 if none. A 1, 4 or 5 earns another throw.
TAP a glowing piece, then TAP a glowing square. It moves exactly the number thrown, along the S-shaped path.
Land on a lone enemy piece to swap places. Pairs, and pieces on safe houses, cannot be swapped.
Three pieces in a row make a wall that nothing can pass. Every piece must stop on square 26.
Square 27 is the House of Water: it sends a piece back to 15. Leave with exact throws: 5 from 26, 3, 2 or 1 from 28-30.
A refused move shakes and tells you why. Hint shows a good move; Take back undoes yours.
First to bring all five pieces home wins. Beat each level for a star; a new puzzle every day.

title: Sepak Takraw
tagline: Receive. Set. Scissor-kick it over the net.
description: Lead a team of three in sepak takraw, the acrobatic kick-volleyball of Southeast Asia, in real 3D. Choose your receive, your set and your attack, time the kick, and read the block. Five rival teams, a Learn path, Think hints and Watch & Learn.
howToPlay: Tap the court to aim, choose a serve and press SERVE when the ring closes.
Choose which player attacks, then where and how the set goes.
Pick an attack and press SMASH on the ring: roll, sunback, scissor, header or foot.
Choose a single block, a double block or drop back when they set.
Win two sets out of three to 21.

title: Shagai
tagline: Toss four ankle bones, hold the best, gallop the felt trail
description: A dice race inspired by the ankle-bone games of Mongolia. Toss four bones that land as Horse, Camel, Sheep or Goat, hold the ones you like and toss the rest again, then gallop your bone-horse along a winding trail across the steppe. Land on a tailwind, avoid marmot burrows, and flick rivals back. Play one to three computer riders, get Hints, or watch a whole race with Auto Play.
howToPlay: Tap or swipe up on the felt mat to toss four bones.
Each side is worth strides; matching sides earn a bonus.
Tap bones to hold them, then Toss again (up to two more times).
Press Gallop: your bone-horse rides that many stations.
Tailwinds push you on, burrows push you back, and landing on a rival flicks them back.
First to station 66 wins.

title: Sheepdog Trials
tagline: Whistle a border collie round the flock in 3D
description: Work a lifelike border collie at a hill-pasture sheepdog trial: outrun, lift, fetch, drive through two gates and pen the flock, scored by a judge. Five courses from valley to highland, weather and time of day, Training and Watch & Learn.
howToPlay: Send the dog wide with Come bye or Away to me, then Walk on from behind the flock.
Keep the dog on the balance point: sheep move away from it, along the line.
Rest the dog with Lie down, hold the flock with Stand, then pen them and shut the gate.

title: Shogi
tagline: Japan's game of generals and drops
description: Shogi is the chess-like strategy game of Japan, played on a 9 by 9 board. Its big idea: a captured piece changes sides and can be dropped back on any empty point. Learn in twelve hands-on lessons where you make every move, play five computer levels from Novice to Master as either side, try the quick 5x5 mini board, or pass the phone to a friend. Every refused move is explained, hints tell you why, and a new checkmate puzzle arrives every day. Hand-drawn kaya board and boxwood pieces, large text and reduced motion options. No ads, works offline. Play in 日本語 or English. Full rules built in.
howToPlay: New here? Tap Learn to play: twelve short lessons where you make every move yourself.
TAP one of your pieces: every point it may move to glows. TAP a glowing point to move.
Landing on an enemy piece captures it. Captured pieces wait on your stand under the board.
To drop: TAP a piece on your stand, then TAP an empty glowing point.
Reach the last three rows and you may promote: TAP Promote or Keep.
Not allowed? The piece tries and returns, and a message says why (check, nifu, blocked...).
Win by checkmate. Hint (3 per game) and Take back help you learn.
The puzzle of the day is mate in 1 on weekdays and mate in 3 at the weekend.

title: Shut the Box
tagline: Roll, add, flip. Close the box.
description: The classic tavern dice game of England and France on a lit oak box with brass hinges and bone tiles. Roll two dice, flip down tiles that add up to the total and try to shut them all: low score wins. Classic and Tall boxes, a five-round Duel with the Innkeeper, a Daily Box, hints from an exact solver and Watch & Learn. No clock, no ads, works offline.
howToPlay: Tap the dice tray to roll two dice and add them up.
Tap open tiles that add up to the total. When they match, they flip down by themselves.
Keep rolling and shutting. If no open tiles can make the roll, the box is over.
The numbers on the tiles still open are your score. Lower is better, 0 is a perfect shut box.
Once tiles 7 and up are shut you can roll a single die instead.
Stuck on a choice? Hint shows the best move and your odds of shutting the box.
Duel the Innkeeper over five boxes with the same dice, or play the Daily Box.
Watch & Learn shows the solver playing whole boxes, with Pause and think time.

title: Silk Road Trader
tagline: Lead a caravan from Chang'an to Baghdad and trade your way across Eurasia.
description: A journey and trading game on the old Silk Road, around the year 780. Provision your camels, buy silk, paper, glass, spices, horses and jade where they are cheap and sell them where they are dear, choose your roads and your pace, and meet the people of the road in illustrated encounters where every choice has consequences. Keep a journal of cities, goods and people, watch an expert trader explain each decision, and finish with the best score before the passes close. Painted landscapes, no ads, works offline.
howToPlay: In each city, buy goods that are cheap here and sell goods that are dear here. Prices move as you trade.
Add camels for space, guards for safety, and buy water and provisions for the road.
On the Road tab choose east or west, a route and a pace, then Depart.
Encounters stop the caravan. Each choice shows its cost and the odds of a good result.
Reputation, customs and languages improve your odds and your score.
Watch and Learn plays an opening journey and explains every decision. Tap the lightbulb for a hint any time.
Reach Baghdad, turn back, or settle on the way: the score counts silver, goods and what you learned.
The first 90 seconds of real play are free.

title: Ski Jump Fjord
tagline: Fly the fjord, land the telemark
description: Crouch down the ice track, jump on the lip, hold your skis in the green band against the wind and land a telemark above a 3D fjord. Four hills, a lifelike jumper and real flight physics.
howToPlay: Hold to crouch on the in-run, lift your finger as the ring closes on the lip.
Drag up and down to keep the skis in the moving green band, sideways to level them.
Lift again as the ring closes on the snow to land in a telemark.

title: Snooker: Cue and Frame
tagline: Pot, spin, build the break.
description: Snooker on a fixed table with real ball physics: top spin, back spin, side spin, cushions and pockets. Aim, pull the cue back, pot a red and a colour, and build a break. Play five computer opponents, share the phone, learn the shots in short lessons, or watch two players explain their choices.
howToPlay: Drag on the table to aim; drag in the Fine aim window for small turns.
Drag on the white ball circle to choose top spin, back spin or side spin.
Pull the cue back on the Power strip and let go to shoot.
Pot a red (1 point), then a colour (2 to 7), and keep going; when the reds are gone, pot the colours in order.
A foul gives the other player at least 4 points.

title: Songo
tagline: The sowing game of Central Africa
description: Songo is the classic mancala game of Cameroon, Gabon and the Ekang peoples of Central Africa. Fourteen houses, seventy seeds: sow clockwise and capture any opponent house your last seed brings to two, three or four, with the houses behind it. A protected first house, a leftmost house that cannot be sown thin, and long sowings through the opponent's row make it play unlike other mancala games. Nine hands-on lessons, free Auto Play, five computer levels, two players on one phone and a daily puzzle. Carved wood board, seeds that click and roll. No ads, works offline.
howToPlay: New here? Nine short lessons teach every move, or watch free Auto Play.
TAP one of your houses on the bottom row to sow it. Glowing houses are playable.
Seeds go one per house, clockwise: along your row right to left, then your opponent's row.
If your last seed makes an opponent house hold 2, 3 or 4, you capture it and any chain behind it.
A row's first house is safe from one landing seed; its leftmost house can't be sown thin.
A house with 14 or more seeds goes once round, then only into your opponent's row.
If your opponent has no seeds, put at least seven on their side if you can.
First to capture 40 of the 70 seeds wins; below 40 at the end is a draw. Hint shows a move and why.

title: Spinning Tops Arena
tagline: Wind it. Launch it. Last one spinning wins.
description: A physics duel with turned wooden tops in a lacquered dish. Build your top in the workshop, pull the cord, whip it to speed and watch the spin, the wobble and the clash decide it. Five rivals, three dishes, two players on one device.
howToPlay: Build a top: body, tip, rim weight, spin direction.
Press near your top and drag back, then let go.
Tap when the needle is in the gold to whip the cord.
Watch the clash: a slow top wobbles, a hard hit near the rim sends a top out.
Win two rounds out of three.

title: Sudoku Nine by Nine
tagline: Pure logic, beautifully made. Hints that teach.
description: Classic Sudoku on soft, tactile tiles. Every puzzle has exactly one solution and is graded by the techniques a person needs. Daily puzzle, pencil marks, undo, and hints that explain the logic step by step. Portrait or landscape, phone or tablet.
howToPlay: Fill the grid so every row, column and 3x3 box holds 1 to 9 once.
Tap a tile, then tap a number. Use Pencil for small candidate marks.
Tap the bulb for a hint: where to look, then why it works.
Pick Easy to Master, or play the Daily Puzzle and keep your streak.
Watch and Learn solves a puzzle for you and explains every step.

title: Surakarta
tagline: The looping capture game
description: A Javanese-named strategy game on a carved board of looping tracks. Pieces step one point but capture by racing round the circuits and the corner loops, with every legal route drawn as a glowing trail. Five opponent levels, two players on one phone, Think with a plain-English reason, seven lessons and Watch & Learn. No timers and no ads.
howToPlay: Each side has 12 pieces. Light plays from the bottom and moves first. Capture every enemy piece to win.
Tap a piece, then a free neighbouring point to step one point in any direction.
To capture, select a piece: glowing trails show routes along the circuits, round a corner loop. Tap the piece at the end of one.
A capturing piece may pass over its own starting point, so even a neighbouring enemy can be taken the long way round.
Think shows the best move and why. The eye button rings pieces that can be captured next turn.
Learn teaches loops, circuits, defence and clean captures. Watch & Learn plays a whole game with a Pause button.

title: Sure Sweep
tagline: No-guess minesweeper. Every board solves by logic alone.
description: Sure Sweep is classic mine-clearing with one guarantee: every board can be fully solved by logic, with no lucky guesses required. Tap to reveal, flip the switch to flag suspected mines, and chord through satisfied numbers to clear the board fast. Stuck? A free hint shows you the deduction you missed, and one free Undo takes back a fatal tap. Sea-chart art, a calm teal palette, and colour schemes you can switch anytime. A full in-app Rules page covers every mechanic.
howToPlay: Tap a cell to reveal it.
A number shows how many mines touch that cell.
Flip the Reveal/Flag switch to Flag, then tap a cell to mark it as a suspected mine.
Tap a revealed number when its flags match it to clear the safe cells around it.
Reveal every non-mine cell to win - the board is guaranteed solvable without guessing.
Stuck? Tap Hint for a free forced move while you play.
Lose a board? Tap Undo once to take back the fatal tap and keep going.
Tap the colour button on the title screen or while playing to switch colour schemes - your choice is remembered.

title: Tab: Stick Race
tagline: The four-stick race of Egypt and the Arab world
description: A traditional race-and-capture game played with four tumbling throwing sticks. Bring your stones on with a one, slide them along a carved 28-square path, land on your rival's stones, rest on the star squares and be first home. Five opponent levels, two players on one phone, Think that explains moves with the real chances of the next throws, a Learn course and Watch & Learn. Play in English or Arabic. No timers and no ads.
howToPlay: Each side has three stones in a short game (five or seven for a longer one). Bring every stone home before your rival does.
Tap Throw: four sticks tumble. Flat sides up are your count: none flat is 6, one is 1, two is 2, three is 3, four is 4.
After a 1, 4 or 6 you throw again. A 2 or 3 ends your throws. Keep every count and spend them in any order.
A 1 brings a stone on. Spend a count: tap a stone, then the glowing square. Landing on a rival stone captures it.
A stone on a star square cannot be captured. A stone carried past the last square goes home.
Think shows the best move and why. Learn teaches the rules. Watch & Learn plays a whole game with a Pause button.

title: Table Tennis Rally
tagline: Real 3D table tennis. Spin it, place it, win it.
description: Slide, flick and read the spin in a fast, real 3D table tennis game for one finger. Play 18 opponents, six tournament cups, a ball machine challenge and a coach that explains every shot.
howToPlay: Hold a finger on the table: your paddle slides under it.
Flick up to hit: gentle is a touch, medium is a topspin loop, hard is a fast drive.
Flick down for a push or a chop with backspin.
Tilt the flick to aim, curve it for sidespin.
Read the spin tag on the ball and pick the stroke that suits it.
Games go to 11 and must be won by 2.

title: Taiko Drum Circle
tagline: Hit the centre for don, the rim for ka.
description: A rhythm game for the big drums of Japanese ensemble drumming. Tap the middle of a drum for don and the rim for ka, in time, with two thumbs or more. Learn six original pieces by call and response, then play them while a circle of computer drummers joins in layer by layer as your timing tightens. Free play with a metronome and an echo partner, a Watch and Learn demonstration, a calibration screen, and an in-app Rules page. Lit hand-drawn drums, synthesised sound, no ads, works offline.
howToPlay: Pick a piece, then start with Learn the pattern: the circle plays a phrase and you echo it back.
Notes fall down a lane onto a drum. A red disc is DON: tap the middle of the drum. A blue ring is KA: tap the rim.
Tap when the note reaches the drum. Closer to the beat scores more. Use two thumbs, or more fingers, for several drums.
Play cleanly and more drummers join the circle. Miss and one drops out.
Free play gives you all four drums with an optional metronome and an echo partner.
Watch and Learn plays the whole piece for you. Pause it any time.
Notes early or late? Settings, then Calibrate, and tap along with the pulse.
On a keyboard: A S D F play don on drums 1 to 4, Z X C V play ka, Space pauses.

title: Tangram: Seven Pieces
tagline: Seven pieces. Endless shapes.
description: The classic Chinese seven-piece puzzle, made to feel wonderful. Drag, turn, flip and click the pieces into more than 80 hand-checked silhouettes, from animals and people to the thirteen convex shapes. A Daily Puzzle, stars, a hint that teaches, and Watch & Learn, which solves a puzzle step by step. No timers and no ads.
howToPlay: Fill the dark silhouette with all seven pieces. Pieces may not overlap or leave gaps.
Drag a piece with one finger. Let go near a corner and it clicks into place.
Tap a piece to select it, tap again to turn it 45 degrees, or drag the round handle.
The parallelogram is the only piece that needs flipping: select it and press Flip.
Press Hint to see which piece goes where, press again to have it placed.
Three stars for no hints. Solve eight puzzles in a chapter to open the next.
Watch & Learn plays a puzzle for you, step by step, with time to think.

title: Tarneeb
tagline: The partnership card game of the Levant
description: Tarneeb is the bidding-and-trump trick-taking card game of the Levant. You and a computer partner bid against two computer opponents for how many of 13 tricks your side will take; the winning bidder names trump and leads. Follow suit, take tricks, and score by what you win. Learn in eight hands-on lessons, play four computer levels with hints that explain the reasoning, and solve a new open-hand Daily Deal every day. An in-app Rules page covers bidding and scoring in full. Designed cards with a large-print option, a warm cafe table. No ads, offline, score only.
howToPlay: Four players, two partnerships: you and your partner against two computer opponents.
Bidding: each player bids 7 to 13 tricks or passes. High bidder names trump and leads.
TAP a card to lift it, TAP again (or DRAG it up) to play. You must follow the suit led.
Highest trump wins a trick; with no trump played, highest card of the suit led wins.
Make your bid and your side scores its tricks; fall short and your side loses the bid.
Eight lessons teach following suit, trump, bidding, partnership play and a full hand.
Daily Deal: all hands face up. Only one first card can reach the target; find it, then play it out.
Hint explains a good bid or card with a reason; Undo takes back your last move.

title: Tavla
tagline: The dice game of the coffeehouse
description: Tavla is backgammon as played in the coffeehouses of Turkey, the Arab world, Israel and Persia, also called tawla, shesh besh and takhteh nard. Race fifteen checkers around 24 points, hit lone checkers, build walls and bear off first. Learn in nine hands-on lessons, play four computer levels or a friend on one phone, and solve a new best-move puzzle every day. Hints explain why, undo is one tap, forced moves can play themselves. Optional score-only doubling cube and gammons. Inlaid wooden board, carved checkers, tumbling dice. Large text and reduced motion. No ads, works offline.
howToPlay: TAP the dice to roll them: they tumble and settle.
TAP one of your checkers: the points it can reach glow. TAP a glowing point to move, or DRAG and drop.
Each die is one move; doubles are played four times. You must play as many dice as you can.
You cannot land on a point held by two or more opposing checkers. A lone checker (blot) that is hit goes to the bar.
A checker on the bar must enter first. A refused move explains why in plain words.
When all 15 are in your home board, bear them off. First to bear off all 15 wins; gammons score more.
TAP Undo to take back a move, Hint for a good play and its reason. Single forced moves can play themselves.
New here? Learn to play has nine short lessons. The daily puzzle is the same for everyone.

title: Tavli: Portes Plakoto Fevga
tagline: The Greek coffeehouse trio
description: Tavli is the Greek tables family, played in coffeehouses as three games in turn on one board: Portes hits, Plakoto pins, Fevga blocks and never hits. Play a match to 5 or 7 against a strong offline computer at four levels, or a friend. Fevga is the closest relative of long nard, known as Nard or Nardy across the Caucasus and Persia, and Portes is tavla or tawla elsewhere. Hints explain why, Watch and Learn shows the computer thinking, text up to 300 percent. No ads, offline.
howToPlay: TAP the dice to roll. TAP a checker: the points it can reach glow. TAP a glowing point, or DRAG and drop.
Each die is one move; doubles are played four times. You must play as many dice as you can.
Portes: land on a lone enemy checker to hit it. A hit checker waits on the bar and must enter first.
Plakoto: nothing is hit. Land on a lone enemy checker to pin it under yours until you leave.
Fevga: nothing is hit and any occupied point is closed. One checker per turn leaves the head; no six-point walls.
Bear off all 15 once they are home. First off wins: 1 point, or 2 if the loser had borne off nothing.
A match plays Portes, Plakoto, Fevga in turn until one side reaches 5 or 7 points.
Undo takes back a step, Hint explains a good move, and the round button pauses. Watch and Learn shows the AI thinking.

title: Tennis Court Rally
tagline: Swipe to aim. Release on the ring. Win the set.
description: Lawn tennis, born in England, in real 3D. Press and drag on the court to choose where the ball lands, release as the ring closes, and play games, sets and tiebreaks on lawn, clay or hard courts. Five rival levels, Learn lessons, Think hints and Watch & Learn.
howToPlay: Your player runs to the ball; you choose the shot.
Press and drag on the court: far up is a drive, short is a drop, down is a lob.
Release as the ring closes for a clean strike.
Serve with one gesture: press to toss, drag to aim, release at the top.
Win games and the set against five rival levels.

title: Tiger and Goat
tagline: Four tigers. Twenty goats. One board.
description: Tiger and Goat is Bagh-chal, Nepal's traditional board game. Four tigers hunt twenty goats on a board of 25 points: the goats are slow but many, the tigers few but fast. The game ends only when every goat is captured or every tiger is trapped. Learn in nine hands-on lessons, play either side against four computer levels or a friend on one phone, and solve a new puzzle every day. Win games to earn new boards and a snowy set of pieces. Hand-painted art, large text and reduced motion options. An in-app Rules page covers it all. No ads, works offline.
howToPlay: New here? Tap Learn to play: nine short lessons where you make every move yourself.
Goats go first: tap an empty point to place one. All 20 must be placed before any goat may move.
To move, tap a piece (its legal points glow), then tap where it goes. Goats step one point along a line and never jump.
A tiger steps one point or jumps a goat to the empty point behind it, capturing it. Goats on an edge or with a piece behind are safe.
Move not allowed? The piece tries, comes back, and a message tells you why.
Tigers win by capturing every goat; goats win when no tiger can move. Five captures do not end it. Three repeats is a draw.
Warnings mark goats a tiger could take next. Hint shows a good move (3 per game). Take back undoes your last move.
Beat each level with each side for a star. The daily puzzle is the same for all, longer on weekends. Winning unlocks boards and pieces.

title: Golden Hour Cricket
tagline: Swipe to bat. Flick to bowl. Beat the sunset.
description: A premium cricket game for your phone. Swipe to bat: direction is the shot, speed is the power, timing is everything. Chase targets with real scoring, read the field, take the risky run, bowl with pace, swing and spin, and play backyard house rules like Tippy-Go and Six and Out. Cricket began in England and spread through the Commonwealth, and backyard cricket is a beloved Australian tradition. Original game: every player and ground is invented.
howToPlay: SWIPE when the bowler lets go: the swipe direction is the shot direction on the field.
The moment you start the swipe is your timing: PERFECT or GOOD gives clean contact.
A slow drag is a ground shot; a fast flick goes in the air for a six, but is riskier.
TAP to block. Do nothing to leave the ball.
Read the field on the radar and swipe toward the gaps.
Tap RUN after you hit the ball, and tap again to queue another run. Watch the throw!
In a Full Match you bowl too: pick a delivery, drag the ring, flick to bowl.
Watch Auto Play to see the computer think through every ball.

title: Toguz Kumalak
tagline: The nine-pebble game of the steppe
description: Toguz Kumalak is the traditional sowing game of Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan, part of the mancala family. Eighteen pits, 162 pebbles: lift a pit, sow round the board, capture pits your last pebble makes even, and win one opponent pit for good as your tuz. Learn in ten short hands-on lessons, play the computer at five levels, pass the phone to a friend, and solve a new puzzle every day. An in-app Rules page covers every rule in full. Carved wood, felt and kilim-pattern art, large text and reduced-motion options. No ads, works offline.
howToPlay: New here? Tap Learn to play: ten short lessons where you make every move yourself.
TAP one of your pits on the bottom row. Glowing pits are the ones you can play.
The first pebble stays in the pit; the rest go one per pit, counter-clockwise.
If your last pebble lands in an opponent pit and makes it even, you capture it.
If it makes exactly three, that pit becomes your tuz: every pebble landing there is yours.
One tuz each; never the opponent's 9th pit, never the same number as their tuz.
First to collect 82 of the 162 pebbles wins. Undo takes back a move; Hint shows why.
Daily puzzle: TAP the one pit that takes the most pebbles.

title: Truco Brasileiro: Manilha
tagline: Shout Truco, bluff the table, win with the manilha
description: Truco is one of Brazil's best-loved card games: three cards each, a shouted stake ladder (Truco, Seis, Nove, Doze) and a lot of bluffing. This version has both big regional styles, Paulista (a turned card names the four manilhas) and Mineiro (four fixed manilhas), for two players or as a four-player partnership. The computer opponents truly bluff and remember whether you run; your computer partner sends and reads the traditional table gestures. Hints, full Rules, big text and Auto Play help you learn. Score only: no chips, no wagers, no ads, works offline.
howToPlay: Win two of the three tricks in each hand. Any card is legal: there is no following suit.
TAP a card to raise it, TAP it again to play it, or DRAG it upward. Gold-edged cards are manilhas and beat everything.
Paulista: the turned vira names the manilhas (next rank up). Mineiro: always 4 of Clubs, 7 of Hearts, Ace of Spades, 7 of Diamonds.
On your turn tap TRUCO to raise the stakes. The other team can accept, run or raise again. Bluff if you dare.
When the computer shouts, choose Accept, Run or the next raise. Hint shows your chance of winning the hand.
At 11 points (Paulista) or 10 (Mineiro) your team looks at all its cards and decides whether to play or run.
With four players tap Signal to tell your partner your best card with a face. Opponents may notice.
Race to 12 points. Auto Play on the title screen shows a full match and explains each decision.

title: Tug of War
tagline: Pull on the beat, dig in, outlast them
description: A village rope contest in real 3D. Tap on the chant beat to heave, hold to dig in against rival surges, call the anchor and the coach, and out-last the other team. A bracket of eight teams on six festival grounds, a Daily Pull and two players on one screen.
howToPlay: Tap anywhere as the ring lands on the target to heave on the chant beat.
Keep your finger down after a tap to dig in: it blocks rival surges and wins stamina back.
Tap ANCHOR to halve the rivals' pull, tap COACH when its meter is full for wider timing.
Bring the flag across your line, or hold the lead when the time runs out; win two pulls to win the match.

title: Tumbang Preso: Can Toss
tagline: Knock the can down. Fetch your slipper. Do not get tagged.
description: A traditional street game from the Philippines in real time. Throw slippers at the can as a thrower, or guard it as the taya: stand it up again and tag the runners. Stylised mannequin players, real flight and bounce physics, five computer players, short lessons, hints with the numbers behind them, and a Watch & Learn mode that explains every choice.
howToPlay: Drag on the yard to place the target ring on the can, choose Lob or Skim and press Throw.
When the can falls, the guard has to fetch it and stand it up: that is your time to run for your slipper.
Behind the toe line you are safe. Out in the yard you can be tagged while the can stands.
A tag ends the round, and you keep your role for the whole match.
As the guard, press Fix can, then chase the runner most likely to be caught.

title: Volleyball
tagline: Pick your role. Pass, set, spike and block.
description: Play one of six players on a volleyball team in real 3D: setter, outside hitter, middle blocker, opposite or libero. Run your player, time each touch and aim with a flick while the computer plays the other eleven. Five rival levels, role tutorials, Learn lessons, Think hints and Watch & Learn.
howToPlay: Choose your role, then drag to run your player.
When the ring closes on your player, lift your finger to pass, set, spike, serve or block.
Flick as you lift to aim: left, right, long or short.
Win sets to 25 (win by two); the deciding set goes to 15.
Tap Roles to see the rotation order.

title: Word Game
tagline: Learn English words by playing. Your words, your pace.
description: Word Game is a fast arcade-style vocabulary game. A question appears at the top and three words drift across the screen - tap the right one before it leaves. Choose your own words by school level, kind of word and topic, make a study set and be quizzed on it, and set the pace from a very slow practice speed to a fast sprint. Questions cover synonyms, antonyms, meanings, odd one out, spelling and listening. Words you miss come back for spaced review, your progress is stored only on your phone and you can export it any time. A full in-app Rules page explains every mechanic.
howToPlay: Tap Play for a quick Classic session, or open Words & pace to choose your word levels, kinds of words, topics, question types and speed.
Try the Journey: a campaign from letters and first words up to graduate vocabulary, with stars, checkpoints and a placement check.
A question appears at the top; three words drift in from the right. Tap the right one before it leaves on the left.
Right answers build a combo up to x4. A wrong tap or a miss resets it. The right answer and its meaning flash by after each answer.
Study makes a set of 5 to 100 words with meanings and flashcards, then quizzes you on just those words.
Review brings back the words that are due, so what you miss comes back sooner and what you know comes back later.
Progress shows your streak, daily goal, mastery stages and levels. Your data export gives you a backup or spreadsheet any time.
Tap Watch & Learn for a free demo that plays itself and pauses before every answer so you can guess first.

title: Xiangqi
tagline: The game of the river and the palace
description: Xiangqi is Chinese chess: two armies of sixteen carved pieces face each other across the river, each general guarded inside its palace. Cannons jump to capture, horses can be hobbled, and the generals may never face each other. Learn in ten hands-on lessons, play Red or Black against five computer levels or a friend on one phone, and solve a new checkmate puzzle every day. Play in 中文 with the traditional characters, or in English with Western piece letters. Two board styles, two piece sets, large text and reduced motion. No ads, works offline.
howToPlay: New here? Ten short lessons teach every move, or tap Auto Play to watch a free demo play itself.
TAP one of your pieces: it lifts and its legal points glow. Then TAP a glowing point, or DRAG the piece there.
A red glow marks a piece you can capture. Cannons capture by jumping over exactly one piece.
Move not allowed? The piece tries, comes back, and a message tells you why.
Attack the enemy general so it cannot escape: that is checkmate. If you are in check you must answer at once.
Generals never face each other on an open file. A side with no legal move loses.
Hint shows a good move (3 per game). Undo takes back your move and the reply.
The daily puzzle is the same for everyone: mate in 2 on weekdays, mate in 3 at weekends.

title: Yut Nori
tagline: Korea's four-stick race
description: Throw four carved sticks and race your horse tokens round a paper board on a woven mat. Yut Nori is the traditional Korean game: yut and mo earn extra throws, corner shortcuts cut across the board, tokens stack to travel as one, and landing on a rival sends it back to the start. Learn in ten hands-on lessons, play a cautious, balanced or aggressive computer team, pass the phone between two teams, and try a new daily challenge. Hand-drawn art, sound, large text and reduced motion. No ads, works offline.
howToPlay: New here? Tap Learn to play: ten short lessons where you make every move yourself.
TAP the felt pad, or SWIPE up on it, to throw the four sticks. Flat sides up: 1 do, 2 gae, 3 geol, 4 yut, none mo (5).
Yut, mo and every capture earn another throw. Throws are kept and spent in any order: TAP a throw chip to choose one.
TAP a token, then TAP a glowing point to move. A token starting on a corner may take the diagonal shortcut.
Land on your own token to stack them; land on a rival to capture it and send it back to the start.
Back-do (the marked stick alone) moves a token one step back. Refused taps always tell you why.
Bring all four tokens home first to win. Hints, take back, five computer levels and a daily challenge help you learn.
Keyboard: Space throws, arrows pick token and point, Tab chooses a throw, H hint, U take back.
